tasks.title: Verify the vault-isolation leak stays closed
tasks.note: **FIXED and SHIPPED as v0.22.1 (`e633fcb`, diagnosed by Atlas, committed by Forge, Session 53). The guard caught its own committer on day one.** The test suite had been writing session summaries into Aaron's **real** Obsidian vault: 13 files named `2026-08-31-ob-server-{slug}.md`, 69 bytes each, frontmatter `project: ob-server-Cz4UxZ` with an empty `sessionId` and a body of `test`. Found at `/end` while listing `Summaries/`. **This is a recurrence with the guard already in place** — `tests/setup-env.ts` has set `OPEN_BRAIN_VAULT_DIR` to a temp vault since the 57-file incident in April, and `vitest.config.ts` loads it. **Root cause — CORRECTED after shipping; the first diagnosis named a real hazard but not the producer.** The demonstrated producer is **`npx vitest` run from the REPO ROOT**: there is no `vitest.config.*` above `open-brain/`, so a root-level run discovers the tests by default glob and loads **no config at all** — `setupFiles` never executes, `OPEN_BRAIN_VAULT_DIR` is never set, and the whole suite runs unisolated against the real vault. Forge's cwd had drifted to the repo root mid-session (a mirror-copy `cd`), so its full-suite runs today wrote the 13 files. Proven twice over: from the root the new guard produced **23 failures**; from `open-brain/`, 688/688 and zero new artifacts. *(Atlas's original diagnosis — `index-v2.test.ts:55`, `skill-scan-runner.test.ts:33`, `apoptosis-reachability.test.ts:138` each `delete` the variable in `afterEach` rather than restoring it, so within a reused worker every later test falls through `paths.ts` to `join(homedir(), …)` — is a **real second path to the same leak** and is also closed by the fix, but it was never shown to have produced a file. Recorded rather than deleted: two independent routes to one silent failure is the point, not a tally of who was right.)* `server.test.ts:16` is the writer in both routes — it runs session-end against `mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "ob-server-"))` and `writeSummary` deposits a summary named for the temp project. **Same invariant as the day's other four instances:** an unset `OPEN_BRAIN_VAULT_DIR` *means* "use production", so absent and configured are the same value from inside the resolver and the guard's own removal is unobservable. **Fix, two parts:** (1) `setup-env.ts` re-asserts the override in a global `afterEach`, so no teardown can leave a worker unprotected whatever it does to the variable; (2) `obsidianVaultDir()` throws when running under vitest and the path resolves to the *real* home vault — a synthetic home is still allowed, so `paths.test.ts`'s deliberate fallback assertion is untouched. Structural prevention plus a loud failure, per the v0.15.1 precedent that removing a read is not the same as counting what you no longer read. **Evidence it holds:** typecheck clean, **688 tests / 49 files green** (+1 = the new test pinning the leak), and a full suite run produced **zero** new `ob-server` files. The 13 artifacts were deleted (Aaron approved); 154 legitimate summaries remain. **What is owed next session:** confirm zero `ob-server-*` in `~/Obsidian Vault v2/Summaries/` after a fresh full run from `open-brain/`. **Revised on the /sync question** — the earlier "no check needed" was wrong, because it assumed the throw always runs, and the root-run route is precisely the case where it does not (no config, no setup, and until v0.22.1 no failure either). Two follow-ups, both filed separately: a `/sync` counter for `ob-server-*` in the vault (there is a preventer and still **no detector** — this was found by accident while listing `Summaries/` at `/end`, not by any check), and a root-level vitest config-or-refuse so a root run fails as one clear message instead of 23 scattered ones. **Also noticed, not fixed:** the artifact filenames lowercase (`ob-server-cz4uxz.md`) while the frontmatter preserves case (`ob-server-Cz4UxZ`) — invisible on Windows, two identities on Linux/macOS, the same blind spot already filed against `ob_store` deriving vault folder names from a canonicalized path. (Session 53)

tasks.title: `ob_store` derives the vault folder from a canonicalized path, so it lowercases the project name
tasks.note: (Session 49). `server.ts:537` computes `projectName = effectiveProject.split("/").pop()` from the *canonical* `project_dir`, and `canonicalizeProjectDir` lowercases the **entire string** when it starts with a drive letter — not just the drive. Result: `ob_store` writes `Experiences/self-improving-agent/` while the `store()` pipeline given an explicit project name writes `Experiences/Self-Improving-Agent/`. **Two live rows already differ** — #235 (older) and #365 (stored during this close-out). **Invisible on Windows** because the filesystem is case-insensitive, so both resolve into the one real folder, `checkVaultIndexParity` passes, and nothing dangles. On macOS or Linux this silently creates a **second project folder**, which `skill-scan` reads as a separate project and which reproduces the exact 60-duplicate divergence repaired earlier this same session. The general rule it violates: **a canonical form is for comparison, not for display** — deriving a human-facing name from a lossy identity key reuses a transformation for a purpose it was not built for. Fix: carry the display name separately (the caller already knows it) rather than reconstructing it from the key; then repoint the two existing rows. Related to the P3 cross-platform item — this is a second Windows-only blind spot. Now documented as §10 of the `path-normalization` skill.

tasks.title: Shadow merge gate: the runtime records what it would have done at each merge, and disagreements with Aaron are counted
tasks.note: DERIVED FROM THE AUTONOMY RULING (see the decision recorded this revision). At every point where a merge to master could occur, the runtime writes a would-merge / would-not-merge verdict with its reasons — deterministic check results, QA E_t status, and once the gates exist, their typed answers — into artifacts/iterations/tNNN/. Aaron still merges. The runtime then records his actual decision beside its own, and the count of disagreements is the instrument that decides when the human gate is removed. BELONGS TO SLICE TWO OR LATER, not Loop 15: it needs the gates to have an opinion, and it needs the merge point to exist in the runtime first. NOT RULED AS THE NEXT LOOP'S SUBJECT. Design constraints that come from the record: the verdict must be written BEFORE Aaron decides, so it cannot be fitted to his answer; both verdicts carry the candidate SHA and a timestamp; a run where the runtime could not form a verdict (gate unreachable, evidence missing) is recorded as UNDEFINED and never as agreement. Zero disagreements across loops with NO real defects in the stream is not evidence of anything — the count only means something when the loops contained failures a gate could have caught.

gaps.what: THIS GAP CORRECTS T-151's CLOSE NOTE AT REV 32 AND CANNOT BE WRITTEN INTO IT - a close note is write-once, so a wrong one is uncorrectable in place and only a pointer like this one can reach a reader of it. (2) THE REAL DEFECT: a working-tree copy can disagree with the repository on line endings while git reports clean, and no check sees it. .gitattributes normalises on commit, so git STORES docs/loops/sia-mailbox-decisions.md as LF and `git show HEAD:<path>` returns LF; because `text eol=lf` makes git compare NORMALISED content, a stale CRLF working copy also reads clean in `git status` and in every diff. The repository is correct, one working tree is stale, nothing in the normal workflow reports the difference, and it survives until something forces a re-checkout of that path. A scripted multi-line edit against that file would hit exactly the mismatch the watch-out warns about, ON A FILE GIT SWEARS IS FINE.
gaps.evidence: Measured 2026-09-17 across three worktrees sharing one .git, same tracked path docs/loops/sia-mailbox-decisions.md: planner 281,558 bytes / 0 CR; main 281,558 / 0 CR; forge 285,228 / 3,670 CR. 281,558 + 3,670 = 285,228 exactly, so the byte delta IS the carriage returns. Found by Forge flagging that its OWN earlier claim was wrong, having generalised from three measured files to a directory of 21; two instruments disagreed in its tree - `file` said CRLF, a grep for a carriage return said 0 - and `file` was right, settled by a byte count, with its detector validated against a known-CRLF file before any negative was trusted. The planner seat re-measured with an independently self-tested detector (probe written with known CR bytes, asserted before use) and found 0 CR across all 19 files in ITS tree. BOTH MEASUREMENTS WERE CORRECT AND BOTH CLAIMS WERE WRONG: the disagreement was never about the file, it was about which checkout, and neither claim carried its scope. Resolved by comparing the trees directly rather than declaring one measurement the winner.

(b) THE TREE-AWARE MESSAGE MAKES IT WORSE: run through MCP against a linked worktree, build-freshness prints 'the hooks and MCP server run from the MAIN checkout's build and are unaffected by this one' — a reassurance ABOUT THE VERY PROCESS THAT PRODUCED IT, asserted rather than measured, and false at the time it was printed because the main build was eleven commits behind. The wording added on 2026-09-19 to make the message true per-checkout is what makes this instance misleading.
gaps.evidence: Reproduced independently by both seats. Planner measurement: `git rev-parse --short HEAD` = e65f251 in the main tree; `build-info.json` commit = e65f251; `git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/master` = 11; `sync --check` run against that tree with a current CLI returns build-freshness [pass]. The misleading reassurance was observed in an ob_sync call through the reconnected MCP server against the planner worktree at the same time. Developer measurement (session 64, G-033 as originally written): pre-reconnect ob_sync returned 23 passed with module-boundary, gitnexus-index and build-freshness ABSENT rather than failing; post-reconnect, 26 passed with all three, and build-freshness caught a real mismatch on its first run. OPENED AS ITS OWN GAP RATHER THAN AMENDING G-033 so the developer's original narrower claim stays auditable and the two extensions are attributable to where they were found.

Read THAT tree's build-info.json and HEAD, compare both to the upstream ref, and report three distinct states rather than two — current, consistently-old, and mismatched. Then the sentence about the hooks and the MCP server is measured rather than claimed, and a consistently-old main tree stops reading as green. decisions.title: Amendment vocabulary: which state records can be corrected, and which are append-only
decisions.note:
Decided once rather than one op per incident. The op union grew by accident — update_task exists because someone needed it, update_gap did not because nobody had yet — and Loop 5 hit the consequence twice in one night.

RULE: a record is amendable when its text DESCRIBES SOMETHING STILL BEING LEARNED. A record is append-only when its text IS THE HISTORICAL FACT, so that editing it destroys the thing the record exists to preserve.

Per type:
- TASKS — amendable (open/update/close/reopen). Title and priority are current intent, which legitimately changes. Already correct.
- GAPS — amendable. A gap describes something we do not yet understand, so its text is provisional by construction. The record most needing correction was the one that could not be corrected. IMPLEMENTED this loop: update_gap. The prior workaround (close + re-add) silently minted a new id and reset opened_session, losing the history the gap list exists to keep.
- VERIFIED — claim append-only; evidence appends; status reopens. The claim is what evidence was gathered against, so editing it invalidates that evidence silently while leaving it attached. Already correct; no update_verified.
- DECISIONS — append-only. A decision log records what was decided and when; amending it is not a correction but a rewrite of the record. Supersede with a new decision instead. Already correct; no update_decision. Gap: decisions carry no supersedes field (tasks do), so superseding is convention only.
- OBJECTIVE / HANDOFF / LAST_SESSION — singletons, set wholesale. Already correct.
- PROJECT.VERSION — REMOVE; do not add set_version. No consumer treats it as authoritative: cli.ts:427 and session-start/state-render.ts:14 display it, state-import/index.ts:439,494 copy it, drift-detector.ts:9 + checks-state.ts:73 + checks.ts:783 compare it to package.json and complain, and state-writer.ts:166 prefers package.json with this only as fallback. It is a cached copy of a truth held elsewhere, with a drift branch and two checks existing solely to police the cache. DEFERRED to Loop 7: 7 call sites plus schema, a state.json migration and test updates is larger than the decision.

ID SCHEME, observed while filing this: the Planner's brief assumed the next ADR id was free, but ADR-021..ADR-026 already exist and nextId has since minted D-001..D-003 alongside them, so the list now carries both schemes. This decision took an explicit ADR-027 to avoid widening the split. The generation bug itself stays filed under G-005 — it is an id question, not an amendment one.

decisions.title: No ranking constant changes on one measured alternative beating one incumbent
decisions.note:
Loop 6's repaired instrument made the recency question answerable and recency_strong (0.02/day) was the only strategy to beat live — 21-11-5, +0.0153 nDCG, winning against a presentation bias that favours the incumbent. The constant was still NOT changed.

Reasoning: recency_strong tests ONE alternative point against ONE incumbent. That 0.02 beats 0.005 is evidence the constant is too low. It is not evidence that 0.02 is right — nothing between or beyond was measured, and the optimum could be anywhere above 0.005. Adopting the one other number that happened to be guessed in the strategy list is the 'flipped because the new number is bigger' outcome the loop's own precondition rules out, and it rules it out whether or not the bigger number won.

shadow/index.ts states the same contract independently: changing production constants stays a human decision; the harness only supplies the evidence. The evidence is now worth supplying, which it was not before this loop.

Recommended next measurement: a sweep — 0.01 / 0.02 / 0.04 as separate strategies — to find where the gain turns over. Adoption is Aaron's call.

What the same run did NOT license: no_maturity ties live, and that must not be read as 'maturity boosts are harmless'. See G-013 (feedback_log 31% complete) and G-014 (success_rate ignores neutral).

decisions.title: ADR-029 - Keep session-start retrieval; suspend the maturity lifecycle; leave the causal question unasked
decisions.note: Loop 7's deliverable, RECOMMENDED not yet adopted - Aaron rules (T-129). 'Does injection earn its place' was three questions wearing one coat, and bundling them is what nearly retired the cheap half on evidence that only ever concerned the expensive half. STEM Agent's argument is that a maturation lifecycle belongs on an EXECUTABLE unit because only an execution yields an objective outcome; that indicts success_rate, maturity and apoptosis on knowledge entries and says nothing about whether fetching a note is worthwhile. A bookmark is not improved by a promotion ladder. Keep retrieval: the case against it was a claim retracted in the vault 26 minutes after it was written, and the first adequately powered contrast this project has produced runs in its favour (start 0.337 vs explicit 0.259 per-entry, n=109 and n=56, opposite to the pre-registration's own selection-bias prediction). Per prereg §5 that is not evidence injection helps - it refutes the claim that injection is the low-value mode. Suspend the lifecycle: success_rate is near-two-valued (98% of rated entries read exactly 1.0), apoptosis cannot fire on arithmetic (needs >=4 harmful on one entry, observed max 1), no_maturity tied live in Loop 6, and the ladder is a ratchet. Recency decay by contrast IS validated, so this is not 'ranking is worthless'. The causal question: control arm named concretely (randomised withhold flag in sessions at ob_start plus a non-self-reported outcome) and then argued against on the pre-registration's own costing - at ~2 sessions/week no effect smaller than enormous is resolvable.

decisions.title: ADR-030 - A bug fix that revives a dead code path ships gated off

Rows produced after the fix are out of sample for Loop 7, the population having been fixed before the change. Secondary rule, and the part that was nearly missed: with the gate closed an unjudged entry is SKIPPED, not recorded neutral - a fallback neutral is indistinguishable from a rater's considered 'retrieved and not used', so the cheaper diff would have destroyed the only signal the corpus still has while appearing to strengthen the data.

decisions.title: ADR-031 - a sign-off transfers across an amend only when the amend is provably disjoint
decisions.note: Refines 'a sign-off does not transfer across an amend', which made every post-QA prose fix cost a re-QA and therefore made the cheap path be not fixing prose, or amending quietly. New rule: it transfers when the amend is provably disjoint from what was signed, and PROVABLY MEANS A DIFF THE QA SEAT CAN RUN - in practice `git diff --stat <signed-sha> HEAD -- <executable paths>` handed over showing empty. Paired with the error-table admission rule: the table records a wrong claim that reached an artifact, a commit, a counterpart or Aaron; a near-miss caught in-process by its own author goes in a separate register as an instance of a named family, never numbered. THE DIVIDING LINE IS ESCAPE, NOT SEVERITY. Both rules exist to stop a correctness rule taxing the behaviour it wants - a rule that adds a row every time someone checks their own work makes checking your own work look like failure. Requested by the seat that stood to benefit from the looser rule, after noticing it had already drafted the entry before asking.

decisions.title: Loop 13's C4 closes as a recorded failure
decisions.note: Ruled by Aaron in-session to the planner seat (Atlas), 2026-09-17, in the words 'yes, Loop 13's C4 closes as a recorded failure'. C4 asked whether core installs and runs with Node and git alone, memory absent. It does NOT, and the reason is the finding: THE MACHINERY IS INSTALLABLE; THE INSTRUCTION IS NOT. Forge ran a real install - fresh clone, npm install --omit=optional, better-sqlite3 confirmed ABSENT before anything ran, env vars pointed at nonexistent paths - and everything mechanical passed: install, build, sync --check (21 passed, 4 skipped, the three memory checks SKIPPING WITH THE REASON rather than passing), open-brain start exit 0, cli-bootstrap.js exit 0 with project detected and agent identity read. server.js died correctly, because it IS the memory half. The loop fails at the instruction layer only. Aaron ruled ONLY that the command surface and hook installation are not Loop 13's work. He did NOT rule them as the next loop's subject; that is recorded as an open task with its derivation, not as a decision. A loop that ends in an honest no is not a failed loop, and the brief was written to make this outcome reportable: it either passes or it does not, and there is no partial credit to hide in.

decisions.title: The HoH loop is autonomous inside a branch; Aaron holds master until the shadow-gate count says otherwise
decisions.note: Ruled by Aaron in-session to the planner seat, by returning the planner's recommendation verbatim: 'autonomous inside a branch, you at master, with the runtime recording what it would have done at each merge so your disagreements become a count. The day that count is zero across loops with real defects in them, remove the gate on evidence.' THIS RESOLVES THE CONFLICT RECORDED IN docs/HOH-JEV.md §6.2 AND docs/loops/loop-15-brief.md §5.1: hoh_jev.md specified a loop that never blocks on a human, which was incompatible with 'Aaron merges, on his word', a rule that has held for every loop in this record. WHAT IS AUTONOMOUS: the plan gate, the developer done-gate, QA scoring, retry, and rollback — closed questions with criteria written in advance, run by the runtime without a human. WHAT IS NOT: the merge to master. The runtime stops at a candidate commit and never merges, pushes to master, or tags. WHY THE MERGE STAYS HUMAN, ON EVIDENCE RATHER THAN NERVES: every serious defect found recently passed the automated checks and was caught by a human question or a human-ordered real run — the retirements check green through five merged PRs then 115 findings in the main tree; build-freshness shipped with its author's tests green and wrong in two checkouts of three; the main tree fifteen commits stale and reporting pass. A gate is a calibrated judge of the evidence it is shown, and every one of those failures was in the evidence, not the judgement. TypeSafe's own words: typed output guarantees the interface, not truth. THE EXIT CRITERION IS MEASURABLE: the runtime records, at every merge decision, what it WOULD have done. Aaron still merges. Each time his decision differs from the runtime's is counted. When that count is zero across several loops that contained real defects, the human gate is redundant and is removed — on evidence. If it is not zero, the count is exactly what would have been lost. This is 'see it red before you trust it green' applied to the human gate itself. WHAT NO GATE REPLACES, stated so it is not quietly automated later: asking the question nobody wrote down. Jev answers questions it is asked; the observation that Loop 14 was briefed against a world that no longer existed came from a person noticing, not from a gate.

handoff.pick_up: Loop 15 runs before Loop 14, ruled 2026-09-19. Loop 14 is re-briefed rather than deferred: it was written when there were two seats and no runtime, and Loop 15 adds the component that would own the artifacts Loop 14 planned to design by hand. There are three seats now — Forge (developer), Atlas (planner), Probe (qa, read-only, evaluates a frozen SHA it did not build). Loop 13 shipped v0.39.0 and v0.40.0 and closed C4 as a recorded failure: the machinery is installable, the instruction is not.
watch_out: LOOP 15 FIXES BOUNDARY FAILURES, NOT MEASUREMENT FAILURES. Eleven near-misses in two days were agents misreading their own instruments. A runtime cannot stop a seat running a grep that hides the line it needed. Do not let the runtime's existence become a reason to trust an unread output.

AN AUTHOR'S GREEN IS WHERE EVALUATION STARTS, NOT A SUBSTITUTE FOR IT. build-freshness shipped asserting a consequence true in one checkout of three with its author's tests passing. Hand Probe a frozen SHA and the deterministic results, then stop.

FAIL CLOSED. Every instrument that failed this project failed open. The one bug that surfaced loudly — cmd.exe eating ^ in <sha>^{commit} — did so only because an undefined distance is an ISSUE rather than a zero. Use execFileSync with an args array; no shell.

A FINDING REPORTED AGAINST A LINE IS USUALLY A FINDING ABOUT A CLASS. The stale-build consequence was reported against one line and an identical instance sat one branch away, in the message firing on the main tree. Look for the sibling before fixing the instance.

EVERYTHING BETWEEN gitnexus:start AND gitnexus:end IN CLAUDE.md IS REGENERATED BY THE ANALYZER. Edits inside it are discarded silently. Anything that must survive a reindex goes above the marker. Do not remove .gitnexusrc — without noStats the analyzer rewrites the tracked file on every run.

A PUSH NEEDS AUTHORITY FOR THAT PUSH, NOT AUTHORITY FOR THE ACTIVITY. This seat pushed a branch nobody had authorised because it had a good reason. A good reason is not authorisation. Whether unauthorised ACTS belong in an error table that counts wrong CLAIMS is unruled.

ACT ON A RELAY ONLY WHERE ACTING NARROWS SCOPE AND STAYS REVERSIBLE, AND RECORD IN THE ARTIFACT WHICH AUTHORITY YOU ACTED ON, AT THE MOMENT YOU ACT. Both halves of the first clause are judgements the actor makes about its own action; the second clause is what makes it auditable.

TWO MEASUREMENTS THAT DISAGREE MAY BOTH BE RIGHT — the resolution is a third measurement, not an argument. A tracked file measured 0 CR in two worktrees and 3,670 in a third, and the byte delta was exactly the carriage returns (G-031). A derived number must carry the ref and time it was derived from.
